# Spook triggers

Use these in the new-style syntax: `trigger: spook.<name>`, with fields under `options:` and the target under `target:`.

### `spook.all_of`: All of these happened

Fires when every one of several triggers has fired inside the same window of time, in any order. Home Assistant's own triggers are a list where any one of them is enough; this is the other one.

Options:

- `triggers` (required, trigger): The triggers that all have to have fired. Order does not matter, and a trigger firing again replaces its earlier turn rather than counting twice.
- `within` (required, duration): How close together they have to be. The window slides, so a trigger that fired longer ago than this is forgotten while the others carry on counting. Example: `00:05:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#all-of-these-happened

### `spook.automation_turned_off`: Automation turned off

Fires when somebody, or something, turns an automation off. Leave the target empty to watch every automation.

Target: `automation` entities, or the devices, areas, floors and labels holding them.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#automation-turned-off

### `spook.condition_met`: Condition turned true

Fires when a condition goes from false to true, using the same condition building blocks as anywhere else.

Options:

- `condition` (required, condition): The condition to watch.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#condition-turned-true

### `spook.cron`: Cron schedule

Fires on a crontab schedule, for the times Home Assistant's own time triggers cannot express, like every weekday at seven or the last Friday of the month.

Options:

- `schedule` (required, text): A crontab expression with five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Supports ranges and steps, and the day-of-week extensions, so "MON#2" is the second Monday and "5L" the last Friday. Nicknames like "@daily" are not supported. Example: `0 7 * * 1-5`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#cron-schedule

### `spook.debounce`: Once it settles

Fires once a trigger has stopped firing for a while, so a burst of them arrives as one. A motion sensor does not report motion once, it reports it twenty times.

Options:

- `triggers` (required, trigger): The triggers to wait out. Any of them firing starts a burst and any of them firing again keeps it going, so several triggers are collapsed together rather than one at a time.
- `for` (required, duration): How long it has to have been quiet before this fires. Every firing starts that wait over, so something that never stops firing never gets reported. Example: `00:00:30`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#once-it-settles

### `spook.device_added`: Device added

Fires when a new device is added to Home Assistant, like a plug that was just paired.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#device-added

### `spook.device_discovered`: Device discovered

Fires when Home Assistant discovers something new it could set up, like a device that just turned up on your network.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#device-discovered

### `spook.flapping`: Entity will not settle

Fires when an entity changes state more often than it should within a stretch of time.

Target: any entities, devices, areas, floors or labels.

Options:

- `changes` (required, number, 2 to 1000): How many changes of state it takes before this fires. Changes of attribute do not count, and neither does an entity appearing or disappearing. Example: `5`.
- `within` (required, duration): The stretch of time those changes have to fall inside. It slides along, so this is always about the most recent changes. Example: `00:05:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#entity-will-not-settle

### `spook.integration_added`: Integration added

Fires when an integration is added to Home Assistant, whoever or whatever added it.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#integration-added

### `spook.integration_failed`: Integration failed to set up

Fires when a configuration entry has been unable to set itself up for a while, past the point where Home Assistant's own retries would have sorted it out.

Options:

- `for` (required, duration): How long an entry has to keep failing before this fires. Home Assistant retries a failing entry every ten minutes at the slowest, so anything shorter than that reports trouble that may still fix itself. Example: `00:15:00`.
- `entry_id` (optional, config_entry): Limit this to particular configuration entries. Leave it empty to watch every one of them.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#integration-failed-to-set-up

### `spook.position_reached`: Position reached

Fires when a cover or valve gets to a position, or moves past it. One that is already there, or comes back from unavailable at it, does not count.

Target: `cover` or `valve` entities, or the devices, areas, floors and labels holding them.

Options:

- `position` (required, number, 0 to 100 %): The position to reach, from 0 (closed) to 100 (open). Example: `30`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#position-reached

### `spook.recovered`: Entity came back

Fires when an entity comes back after having been unavailable for a while, so a router rebooting does not read as everything in the house recovering.

Target: any entities, devices, areas, floors or labels.

Options:

- `for` (required, duration): How long the entity has to have been away before coming back counts. Anything shorter is a flicker: reloading an integration takes every one of its entities through unavailable and back inside a second. Example: `00:15:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#entity-came-back

### `spook.repair_issue_created`: Repair issue created

Fires when a new repair issue turns up, so you can hear about one without visiting the repairs page.

Options:

- `domain` (optional, text, one or a list): Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them. Example: `hue`.
- `severity` (optional, list, each one of `critical`, `error`, `warning`): Limit this to issues of a particular severity. Leave it empty for all of them.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#repair-issue-created

### `spook.repair_issue_removed`: Repair issue resolved

Fires when a repair issue goes away, either fixed or no longer reported.

Options:

- `domain` (optional, text, one or a list): Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them. Example: `hue`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#repair-issue-resolved

### `spook.script_started`: Script started

Fires when a script starts a run. A run the script refuses, because it is already running, does not count. Leave the target empty to watch every script.

Target: `script` entities, or the devices, areas, floors and labels holding them.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#script-started

### `spook.sequence`: Triggers in order

Fires when several triggers happen one after another, in the order given.

Options:

- `steps` (required, trigger): The triggers that have to happen, in order. Only the one being waited for is listening, so a later step firing early is not a match.
- `timeout` (optional, duration): How long the whole sequence may take, counted from the first step. Left out, it waits indefinitely. Example: `00:02:00`.
- `reset` (optional, trigger): Triggers that abandon a sequence already under way, putting it back to waiting for the first step.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#triggers-in-order

### `spook.stale`: Entity fell silent

Fires when nothing has written to an entity for a while, which catches a device that died quietly rather than going unavailable.

Target: any entities, devices, areas, floors or labels.

Options:

- `for` (required, duration): How long an entity has to stay silent before this fires. An entity that keeps reporting the same value is not silent. Example: `01:00:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#entity-fell-silent

### `spook.state_changed`: Spook's state trigger

Fires when an entity changes state, for everything a target covers: entities, devices, areas, floors and labels. Narrow it down by domain, integration or device class, or leave the target empty and let those pick the entities from everything. Exclude things again, and decide how long a change has to hold before it counts.

Target: any entities, devices, areas, floors or labels.

Options:

- `domain` (optional, text, one or a list): Only entities of these domains, like binary_sensor or cover. Without a target, picks them from everything. Example: `binary_sensor`.
- `integration` (optional, text, one or a list): Only entities provided by these integrations, like zha or hue. Without a target, picks them from everything. Example: `zha`.
- `config_entry` (optional, config_entry): Only entities of this integration entry. Without a target, picks them from everything.
- `device_class` (optional, text, one or a list): Only entities of these device classes, like door or window. Without a target, picks them from everything. Example: `door`.
- `exclude_target` (optional, target): Entities, devices, areas, floors or labels to exclude. Everything in them is excluded, the diagnostic entities too.
- `exclude_domain` (optional, text, one or a list): Exclude entities of these domains. With nothing in Exclude, this applies to everything the target covers. Example: `sensor`.
- `exclude_integration` (optional, text, one or a list): Exclude entities provided by these integrations. Example: `template`.
- `exclude_config_entry` (optional, config_entry): Exclude the entities of this integration entry.
- `exclude_device_class` (optional, text, one or a list): Exclude entities of these device classes. Example: `battery`.
- `attribute` (optional, text): Follow this attribute instead of the state. Example: `brightness`.
- `from` (optional, text, one or a list): Only changes coming from one of these states. Example: `off`.
- `not_from` (optional, text, one or a list): Only changes not coming from one of these states.
- `to` (optional, text, one or a list): Only changes going to one of these states. Example: `on`.
- `not_to` (optional, text, one or a list): Only changes not going to one of these states.
- `ignore_unavailable` (required, boolean): Leave out changes from or to unavailable and unknown, so a restart or a router reboot does not fire for everything. Turn off to use them in From or To. Default: `true`.
- `attribute_changes` (required, boolean): Also fire when only an attribute changed and the state stayed the same. Does nothing while following an attribute. Default: `false`.
- `behavior` (required, automation_behavior): Fire for each entity, for the first one of the target to get there, or once all of them are there. First and all need To or Not to. While unavailable and unknown are ignored, entities in those states do not take part. Default: `each`.
- `for` (optional, duration): Only fire once the new state has held for this long. Any other change in between calls it off. Example: `00:05:00`.
- `blip_tolerance` (optional, duration): While waiting out For, going unavailable or unknown and coming back as it was within this time does not start the wait over. Only works together with For. Example: `00:00:30`.
- `delay` (optional, duration): Wait this long before firing, whatever happens in between. Like a delay at the start of the actions. Example: `00:01:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#spooks-state-trigger

### `spook.target_temperature_reached`: Target temperature reached

Fires when the temperature of a thermostat or water heater reaches its target, or jumps past it. Changing the target does not count, and neither does a device that is off.

Target: `climate` or `water_heater` entities, or the devices, areas, floors and labels holding them.

Options:

- `tolerance` (optional, number, 0 to 10): How close to the target still counts as there, in the device's unit. For a thermostat that settles just short of its setpoint. Zero means the target itself. Default: `0`. Example: `0.5`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#target-temperature-reached

### `spook.update_installed`: Update installed

Fires when an update entity reports a different installed version, whether somebody pressed install, the device updated itself, or it was updated outside of Home Assistant.

Target: `update` entities, or the devices, areas, floors and labels holding them.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#update-installed

### `spook.user_added`: User added

Fires when somebody is given a login to Home Assistant. Users Home Assistant creates for its own integrations are left out.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#user-added

### `spook.watchdog`: Watchdog

Fires when something that was expected to happen does not happen in time.

Options:

- `arm` (required, trigger): What starts the watch. The wait is measured from here, and arming again while already waiting starts the wait over.
- `expect` (required, trigger): What is expected to follow. Arriving in time calls the watch off, and nothing fires.
- `within` (required, duration): How long the expected thing has to arrive. This fires when that time passes and it has not. Example: `00:02:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#watchdog

### `spook.while`: While a condition holds

Fires when a condition turns true, and keeps firing on an interval for as long as it stays true.

Options:

- `condition` (required, condition): The condition to watch. Firing starts when it turns true and stops when it stops being true.
- `every` (required, duration): How long to wait between one firing and the next, for as long as the condition holds. Example: `00:10:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#while-a-condition-holds
